contributions: Open Educational Resource covering graph neural networks from first principles to frontier topics
Learning graph of 300 interconnected concepts organized across 15 taxonomy categories
37 interactive p5.js MicroSims for hands-on manipulation of GNN internals
Bloom's-aligned exercises (12 per chapter across all cognitive levels) and 270 quiz questions
Self-contained prerequisite coverage (linear algebra, probability, PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric) in Chapter 0
Full runnable PyTorch Geometric code and up-to-date benchmarks with live leaderboard links
Broad coverage across 27 chapters including graph transformers, knowledge graphs, heterogeneous graphs, scalable GNNs, generative models, and LLM+GNN integration
limitations: The textbook is an early version (0.1) with no registered DOI. It is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, restricting commercial use. It is authored by a single student/independent developer, which may limit breadth of review and potential gaps in coverage. Prerequisites are covered only through Chapter 0; readers without introductory ML background may still struggle. The work does not present novel algorithms or empirical benchmarks but rather synthesizes and teaches existing methods.
methods: The textbook was authored as a single-developer open-source project using MkDocs Material, p5.js, PyTorch Geometric, and Claude AI. It organizes 300 key concepts into a dependency-aware learning graph so prerequisites are introduced before use. Each chapter follows a consistent pedagogical sequence: real-world motivating example, plain-language intuition before equations, full mathematical derivations, and complete runnable PyTorch Geometric implementations. Interactive micro-simulations are embedded directly in the browser to let readers manipulate GNN parameters and observe behavior in real time.
results: The resource is version 0.1 (last updated May 28, 2026) and totals 301,873 words across 27 chapters. It includes 37 MicroSims, 270 quiz questions distributed over all six Bloom's Taxonomy levels, an annotated glossary of 300 key concepts, an FAQ with 82 common questions, and chapter-level references linking to authoritative primary sources. The text cites industry-scale deployments (Pinterest PinSage on a 3-billion-node graph driving 40% of home-feed impressions; AlphaFold 2 using attention over residue-pair graphs) and documents field growth (arXiv papers with 'graph neural network' rose from under 100 in 2017 to over 7,500 in 2023—a 75× increase). No experimental results are reported; the book is a pedagogical resource, not an empirical study.
tldr: This is an open, interactive intelligent textbook on Graph Neural Networks by Anvith Pothula (2026, v0.1) that provides a self-contained, pedagogically structured resource with 27 chapters, 37 browser-based simulations, and full PyTorch Geometric code to address the gap between general ML curricula and the fast-growing field of graph machine learning.
